source.title: Planning Transformer: Long-Horizon Offline Reinforcement Learning with Planning Tokens

page_placements.theme: Explicit planning modules or planning tokens in RL and sequence agents

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates an explicitly designed and trained offline-RL planning-token architecture. Its results do not test whether next-token language models spontaneously represent future tokens or use such representations.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 compares Planning Transformer performance with Plans enabled and disabled; the text reports improvement but the supplied text does not give the plotted values. Table 1 compares PT with prior methods, and does not isolate the effect of Plans. The paper's planning tokens are deliberately introduced and trained, so these results are not evidence that look-ahead arises without that inducement.
record.test_reason: The paper builds an offline-RL Decision Transformer variant with an explicit planning head trained on future-trajectory targets. The planning is induced by architecture and loss, not measured as arising in a next-token model. It has no language model, no rhyme task and no probe of spontaneous look-ahead, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that prepending model-generated Planning Tokens improves long-horizon offline-RL performance, reaching SOTA or competitive results on D4RL. They say the plans add interpretability through plan visualisations and attention maps. Applying the framework to LLMs is listed as future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is an offline-RL architecture with an explicit planning head trained to predict future trajectory tokens, rather than a test of naturally occurring future-token representations in a next-token language model.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported Plan benefit varies by environment horizon: the text describes a substantial increase on Kitchen-Partial and only a slight increase on hopper-replay.

fits_no_version.finding: Disabling the explicitly trained Planning Tokens lowers the normalized score in every environment shown in Figure 3. The drop is large on long-horizon Kitchen-Partial and slight on hopper-replay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Decision-Transformer offline RL, explicitly trained future-trajectory planning tokens improve performance, more so on long-horizon tasks.

record.problems: The Plan ablation values are presented only in Figure 3 in the supplied text, without recoverable numerical values or uncertainty. The paper reports using 3 random training seeds for PT, rather than 5 for the cited evaluation methodology.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports PT scores against prior methods but does not isolate the effect of Plans. Table 2 reports planning-design ablations, but these do not test the claim versions about spontaneous language-model look-ahead. Figure 3's other plotted environment values are not individually identified in the text provided.

untested.parts: No language model, no verse, no rhyme-word representation or intervention.
No probe of hidden states for future-token decodability.
No test of whether next-token models compute features for later positions.
Planning tokens are explicitly trained, not emergent look-ahead. No reasoning, chess or Sokoban.
No test of whether emergent plans are shallow or incidental.

record.verdict_notes: Engineered multi-token planning in an RL agent (3-layer transformer). It is relevant only as an analogy to planning, not as a test of emergent planning in LMs. The Figure 3 values are not in the text. PT used 3 seeds versus 5 for the cited baselines.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme representation, or intervention on rhyme words.
No language-model hidden-state probe or measurement of future-token decodability.
No test of whether next-token models compute features early because they benefit later positions.
No open-weight language-model rhyme-planning test or attribution-graph/probing analysis.

The paper studies offline-RL planning tokens that are explicitly added and trained, not look-ahead arising in models without that inducement; it does not study multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban.
No test of whether naturally occurring look-ahead is shallow, incidental, or merely a local next-token heuristic.

relation.reason: The paper discusses transformer planning and proposes an explicitly trained planning architecture; it neither tests nor uses the catalog's finding of naturally arising internal look-ahead.

tranche.reason: Sections 3.1–3.3 explicitly construct future-trajectory targets and train a planning head with a plan prediction loss. The ablation tests these engineered tokens, without measuring naturally arising look-ahead.

source_check.notes: Both rows describe the paper's own planning-token ablation and appropriately link to no claim version. The authors' conclusion is accurately summarized; applying PT to language models is future work.
